# Ontobricks import — Clinical Study lab (GENERATED by scripts/ls_graph_build.py; do not edit)

Source scope: **`eli_test_classic_catalog.clinical_study_graph` only**. It holds one view per class (`e_*`) and one per relationship (`r_*`). Don't add `clinical_study_semantic` (metric views abort the scan, as in HEDIS rev 5) or the gold eligibility/population tables (the graph has to derive those itself, ADR-0025).

IRI base: `https://clinical-study-lab.example/ontology`. Class `https://clinical-study-lab.example/ontology#<Class>`, property `https://clinical-study-lab.example/ontology/<name>`, instance `https://clinical-study-lab.example/ontology/<Class>/<ID>`. This is the convention Ontobricks compiles, so the R2RML needs no prefix edits.

Counts: 31 classes with data, 72 relationship views, 61 object properties.

## Steps

1. Create a new Ontobricks project/domain (suggested name **Clinical Study Lab**). Use a separate project, not `clinicaldomain`, so the HEDIS graph and its app pin are untouched.
2. Import the ontology: `src/ontology/life_sciences/clinical_study.owl.ttl`.
3. Import the mapping: `src/ontology/life_sciences/clinical_study.r2rml.ttl`. If the importer rewrites or rejects anything, fix it with the tables below. Each row is one view → one mapping, columns `ID`/`Label` for entities and `source_id`/`target_id` for relationships.
4. Set source scope to the schema above, then build/publish.
5. Send Claude the published triplestore table name (e.g. `eswanson_demo.ontobricks.triplestore_<project>_v1`). Claude runs the graph checks against it.
